title: Iraqw Milk and Millet Drink
localName: Kinywaji cha Maziwa na Mtama — Waaraqw
community: Iraqw people of Mbulu — the traditional cooling drink
author: Mama Salima
desc: Iraqw Milk and Millet Drink — finger millet cooked briefly and mixed with fresh soured milk, chilled and served as a refreshing drink. The Cushitic dairy-grain tradition of the Mbulu Highlands — nourishing, cooling, and deeply characteristic of the Iraqw people.
longDesc: The Iraqw milk and millet drink is a cold preparation — unlike hot porridge, this is a refreshing, chilled drink made from cooked millet gruel thinned with soured milk and served cool. It is drunk throughout the day in the Mbulu Highlands, particularly in the hot dry season.
ingredients: 1 cup natural soured milk or yogurt
steps: Cook millet flour with 2 cups water into a thin, pourable porridge.
Stir in soured milk, honey, and salt.
chefTips: Should be pourable — thinner than eating porridge.
Serve very cold for maximum refreshment.
commonMistakes: Too thick — should pour like a drink.
cookingScience: See TZA253 for the nutritional science of millet and fermented milk combination.
sustainabilityTips: Millet and cattle milk — both produced in the Mbulu Highlands ecosystem.
healthBenefits: High calcium from millet and milk.
culturalNote: Iraqw milk and millet drink is the taste of the Mbulu Highlands afternoon — the cool, slightly sour drink that refreshes after a morning of farming the terraced fields. It carries in one glass the two most important elements of Iraqw food culture: the ancient grain and the cattle milk.
